name: Egoist Anarchism
summary: Egoist anarchism, drawn from Max Stirner's The Ego and Its Own, makes the unique individual's own interest the only standard and denies that state, society, morality, God or humanity has any claim on them. It holds that right is only power, that property is what one can take and keep, and that individuals should deal with each other in shifting voluntary unions of egoists instead of under law or any ruler. It rejects both the state and the moral and collective creeds of liberals, nationalists and communists as spooks.
scope: The egoist strand of anarchism founded on Max Stirner (1844), as taken up by Benjamin Tucker after 1886, James L. Walker's Philosophy of Egoism, and the illegalists. Based mainly on The Ego and Its Own and Walker, supported by SEP and Wikipedia. Excludes the natural-rights individualism of Spooner and early Tucker, anarcho-capitalism, and Nietzschean or social-Darwinist 'might makes right' writers such as Redbeard.

keyFigures.name: Max Stirner
keyFigures.role: Author of The Ego and Its Own, the founding text of egoism.

keyFigures.name: James L. Walker
keyFigures.role: Wrote The Philosophy of Egoism and called himself an egoistic anarchist.

keyFigures.name: Benjamin Tucker
keyFigures.role: Editor of Liberty who adopted egoism and dropped natural rights.
