sources.title: Egoist anarchism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of the strand, Tucker and Walker, unions of egoists applied to sex and romance, relation to illegalism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Stirner never addressed health care; a tax-funded state service rests on a state he calls a despotism, so an egoist would have care arranged by voluntary contract or union.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A legal wage floor is a state command; egoists would leave wages to what each side can win through voluntary contract (inferred from Walker's contract-only order).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Egoists prefer voluntary exchange to state allocation, but Stirner does not praise markets as such and criticizes competition as a new creed; the answer is inferred from Walker's contract-based anarchy.

public-ownership.rationale: Public ownership vests property in the state or society, which Stirner treats as an alien power over the owner; property is what the individual can take and hold.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxes are state exactions imposed under command; an egoist would resist any tax where possible and not endorse a state redistribution scheme.

unions-good.rationale: Stirner prizes free unions of egoists that serve each member, which could include labor combinations, but denies that unions are good for society as such and attacks the workers' collective creed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Stirner rejects property as a sacred right ("what you have the power to be you have the right to"), holding that property is only what one can take and keep, so no right that is hard to override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is the state commanding economic life; egoists reject the state as the proper instrument, though they would not defend corporate privilege either.

cut-welfare.rationale: Egoism has no stake in welfare as a policy: it opposes state coercion but also state-based moral claims; adherents split between ending state programs and not caring.

worker-ownership.rationale: Stirner scorns communist and socialist claims that the earth belongs to those who till it; ownership belongs to whoever can take it, so collective worker ownership is not a principle, though voluntary unions may do it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Egoists see the state as a despotism with no claim on the individual, so state surveillance, whatever the pretext, is an alien power to be evaded.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Ownness means mastering oneself and answering to no law on one's body; egoists reject legal moral restrictions on what individuals do, and illegalists ignore such laws anyway.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Law is an order from a ruling will; egoists reject legal speech restrictions and the sacred moral categories behind them.

strong-leader.rationale: Stirner calls every state a despotism whether of one or many; a leader who commands the country is just another master over the ego.

state-harmful.rationale: Stirner: "Every State is a despotism"; the egoist aims to annihilate the state and replace it with a union of egoists.

limit-guns.rationale: Egoists hold power to be the basis of right and reject state disarmament of individuals, though Stirner did not discuss guns; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and army are the instruments by which the state enforces its will over individuals, which egoism opposes outright.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Egoist anarchists apply the union of egoists to sex and romance and reject moral laws on consensual conduct.

decide-locally.rationale: Egoists prefer smaller voluntary associations to national government, but they do not value locality as such, since a local authority is also a ruler; inferred from voluntary-contract anarchy.

rehabilitation.rationale: Stirner treats punishment as the ruler's right, not the criminal's, and rejects moral reform, since "crime" is defined by power; rehabilitation imposes a moral norm just as punishment does.

traditional-family.rationale: Stirner treats family piety as a sacred tie and fetter and says forming family ties binds a person; traditional structures are not the foundation of anything the egoist honors.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Egoists reject the state's role in marriage altogether but would not forbid it, so they would accept it as a free union without needing legal recognition; inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: The individual owns their body and is bound by no moral or legal duty; egoists would let the woman decide, and reject state prohibition.

more-religion-public.rationale: Stirner treats religion as subordination to a "higher essence" and a spook to be dispelled; egoists want it out of public life and private life alike.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Egoists recognize no duty to correct historical wrongs and reject collective moral obligation, but would oppose racial hierarchy by the state; they would not back organized programs.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Stirner rejects fixed essences like "Man" as spooks, which fits seeing gender roles as imposed ideas, though egoists did not theorize gender as such.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Stirner says the nation takes the patriot's sacrifice and has the profit; "there is no fatherland and no patriotism" for the ego, so preserving the nation is a spook.

gradual-change.rationale: Stirner prefers insurrection of individuals to reform through institutions and does not defer to established institutions; he does not demand speed either.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Borders are state creations and the nation a spook; egoists reject using law to keep individuals out.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of every higher power over the individual; international organisations postdate the doctrine.

free-trade.rationale: Voluntary exchange without state interference suits contract-based anarchy, though egoists do not claim it benefits everyone; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: The nation is a sacred cause egoists reject, so they do not put the country's interests first, but they also reject global cooperation as a duty; they put the self first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: State military action in the name of human rights serves "Man" as a higher essence, a spook, and is carried out by states egoists oppose.

open-borders.rationale: Borders are artificial limits imposed by states; the egoist moves wherever they can, and the nation has no claim on them.

limit-growth.rationale: Egoists reject collective impositions in the name of nature or humanity, so no state limit on growth; Stirner is silent on environmental questions.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Drastic government action is state coercion in service of a collective cause; egoists would not accept it as binding, though they might choose to act for their own reasons.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Egoism says nothing about technology; its adherents are split between technological optimism and skepticism of any new creed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No egoist position exists on energy; individuals would judge by their own interest and a state program has no claim on them.

revolution-justified.rationale: Stirner rejects revolution as the founding of new institutions but approves insurrection by individuals for their own ends, so his view is mixed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Deference to experts or any higher authority is subordination to a spook; egoists answer to their own judgment.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning imposes a ruling will on every producer, the opposite of the union of egoists.

socialized-markets.rationale: Egoists reject state or public ownership as a principle of right, though they would not object to voluntary worker-owned firms; the statement frames ownership as a condition for markets, which egoists do not accept.

land-value-tax.rationale: Stirner says land belongs to whoever can take it; a land tax is a state levy and implies the community owns land.

tax-inheritance.rationale: An inheritance tax is another state exaction; egoists oppose taxation and recognize no community claim on what individuals hold.

basic-income.rationale: A state-paid basic income depends on taxation and a sovereign state; egoists reject both and assert no right to be provided for.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tariffs are state coercion used for national ends; egoists reject both the state and the nation as causes.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state directing the economy is the opposite of egoist anarchy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Egoists hold property by might, with no principle favoring wide distribution; some individualist-anarchists wanted small property, but Stirner mocked the right.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Stirner attacks communism as setting up a new sacred claim and says the producer enjoys what they take; Walker assumes contract and exchange, so abolition of wages is no goal.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Egoists oppose state institutions generally, so a state bank would go, but egoists say nothing on monetary policy; inferred from anti-state and contract views.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies that fix wages and prices subordinate individuals to a collective and the state.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rule by a party guided by an ideology is the sort of possession by a fixed idea and despotism Stirner attacks.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: "Every State is a despotism, be the despot one or many"; no head of state is legitimate over an egoist.

democracy-best.rationale: Stirner calls democracy "anthropocracy" and denies that even a unanimous vote binds the egoist; majority rule is another ruling power.

direct-votes.rationale: Egoists reject being bound by any vote, even a direct one, though they might use a vote as a tool; it is not a principle of theirs.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as a basis of political power would make power a collective right over individuals; egoists reject any such ruling body.

right-to-secede.rationale: A person or group may break from the state at will since no authority binds them, though egoists do not frame this as a right of regions.

natural-rulers.rationale: Egoists deny that anyone has a right to rule, but Stirner holds that the stronger do rule in fact; so no natural right to rule exists.

political-violence-never.rationale: Egoists recognize no moral bar on force: right is power, and Stirner's insurrection and the illegalists accepted violence for their own ends.

war-builds-character.rationale: War for a nation serves a spook, and the patriot's sacrifice profits the nation, but egoists glorify neither peace nor sacrifice; Walker also accepts self-defense.

separate-church-state.rationale: Both are alien powers; egoists would drop both, so strict separation is the minimum they would accept, though the framing keeps a state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Stirner treats scripture and God as sacred spooks and law as an order; an egoist denies both.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Walker allows protection by voluntary combinations against violence; egoists oppose the state but did not endorse private firms as a program, and anarcho-capitalists are a different strand.

military-superiority.rationale: The national state is a spook and an arms race serves it; egoists reject maintaining state power.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The nation and its ethnic composition mean nothing to the ego, which belongs to no collective.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Stirner treats class and humanity as abstractions and attacks the proletarian cause as another idea that possesses people; egoists see individuals' interests, not classes, as the motor.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Stirner rejects equality as a sacred claim: "equal enjoyment alone entitles you to equal enjoyment."

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No group has a right to land; it belongs to whoever can take and hold it, so egoists would not support a collective authority claim.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Egoists recognize no moral debts between collectives and treat rights as power; states owing reparations rests on moral duty.

civilizational-union.rationale: A union of nations based on religion or civilization is another collective cause that egoists reject.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Stirner and Walker ground all conduct in self-interest, but both reject morality and moral duty as such, so they endorse self-interest without calling it morally good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Walker: "Moralistic Duty is the hardened dregs of fear"; Stirner denies duties to community.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Stirner treats the world as property to use and denies sacred essences; he would not grant nature value apart from the owner's interest.

limit-population.rationale: State limits on births are commands over the individual; egoists would oppose such orders but have no stated position on population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Egoism has no critique of industrial civilization as such; a spook-centered analysis does not fit, though some individualists were hostile to modern society.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Egoism offers no stance on the pace of technology; the individual would use or reject it as interest dictates.

human-enhancement.rationale: The ego owns its body and mind and may modify them as it likes; no law or moral rule limits this.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government by algorithms is still government, a ruling will placed over the individual.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Power to shield oneself from the state is something the egoist would claim; privacy against the state is a matter of might.

restore-past-order.rationale: Stirner scorns the sacred and tradition; a lost social order is another spook, and egoism rejects fixed orders.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Egoists judge everything by their own interest, which is akin to results, yet they are consciously committed to a philosophy; split.

direct-action.rationale: Stirner's insurrection and the illegalists' practice put individual action over elections; egoists reject parliaments.

means-match-ends.rationale: Egoists form unions that already embody their aims, but Stirner is not committed to consistency of means with ends; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Egoism has no program on foraging; some egoists, like Novatore, were hostile to civilization but Stirner and Walker were not.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Stirner criticises the communists' claims about labor but has no program on division of labor; voluntary exchange of services in Walker is compatible with it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Stirner rejects distribution by a collective claim; one has what one can take, and "equal enjoyment alone entitles you to equal enjoyment."

production-for-use.rationale: The egoist produces for their own ends, which could be use or profit; Stirner does not call for a collective rule on production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Exploitation as a moral wrong depends on a moral claim to the whole product that Stirner rejects; each takes what they can in contract.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A class dictatorship is rule by a collective over others and attacks the ego; Stirner opposed the communists' claims.

collective-farming.rationale: Compulsory collective farming imposes a collective will on individual cultivators, and Stirner mocked the communist claim that land belongs to the tiller.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist theory of imperialism is outside the egoist framework; Stirner attributes wars to states and sacred causes, not to capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Stirner treats taxes as exactions by a despotic state, but "theft" presupposes a property right he denies; the natural-rights theft language comes from Tucker-style individualists outside the scope.

harm-principle.rationale: Egoists reject the state's authority to restrict adults at all, even for harm; they accept protection from violence by voluntary combination, but not a principled limit.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Stirner denies natural rights to anyone, individual or group, holding that right is only what power secures; so egoists reject the statement though they agree the individual alone matters.

conscription.rationale: The state compelling people to fight is the paradigm of the nation taking the sacrifice; egoists refuse.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The egoist places their own freedom to leave above participation in rule, but egoists reject the state entirely and are not interested in checks on it.

state-as-business.rationale: Egoists oppose the state and do not seek to reform it into a business; voluntary exchange suits them, yet the citizen-as-customer model keeps a state.

positive-liberty.rationale: Stirner distinguishes freedom, which he treats as given by others, from ownness, which one takes; he rejects the idea that society must provide the means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Egoists have no position; Stirner attacked humanist and liberal intellectuals as ideologues but did not weigh their power against elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Egoism takes no position on the origin of group differences, and treats the individual as unique rather than as a racial type.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through any corporate or community body places a collective above the individual.

total-state.rationale: The totalizing state is the despotism egoists oppose.

national-rebirth.rationale: National rebirth is a cause to which individuals are asked to sacrifice, which Stirner rejects.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Expansion of a strong nation serves the state and nation as sacred causes, which egoists reject.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule on oaths of loyalty makes the follower a possession of the lord; egoists reject allegiance to any ruler, though they may form unions of mutual interest.

bound-labor.rationale: Being legally bound to land and lord is subordination that the egoist rejects absolutely.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Stirner treats claims of truth as sacred spooks that rule people, which gives some sympathy, but egoists do not reduce knowledge to who holds power.

universal-morality.rationale: Walker: "I appeal to no Moral law of the world. I recognize none"; Stirner treats universal truths as spooks.

single-common-good.rationale: The common good is a sacred abstraction; egoists hold politics is a clash of individual interests with no single good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Egoists oppose all national states and treat nations as spooks, so a Jewish state would be no exception, though they take no stand on Jewish rights as individuals.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Egoists recognize no rights of nations, and see citizenship as a state device, but they favor free movement; they would not endorse a right tied to national membership.

revive-national-language.rationale: Using the state to impose a language serves the nation as a cause; egoists would leave language to individual use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic votes bind members, which egoists reject; voluntary firms can run themselves any way their members agree.

school-vouchers.rationale: Vouchers are state funding through taxes; egoists oppose the state, though they favor unregulated schooling over state schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Egoism has no fiscal doctrine; deficits and stimulus are both state policy that egoists reject.

economic-freedom.rationale: Egoists want no state rule over exchange, which is close to this; but Stirner treats freedom as less than ownness and makes no claim about political freedom's dependence.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule by a moral example is still rule, and egoists reject moral exemplars as spooks.

national-self-determination.rationale: The nation is a spook and a nation-state is a state; egoists want self-determination only by the individual.

force-without-un.rationale: Egoists oppose state military power in any form and do not care about UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Stirner attacks religion but also treats reason and truth as sacred ideas that possess people; he opposes faith and the worship of reason alike.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Egoists reject citizenship as a source of claims and oppose the state, but they have no principled position on who gets benefits; they oppose welfare as state coercion.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Conditions imposed by state commands are rejected as orders; but egoists recognize no right to welfare either.

class-collaboration.rationale: Egoists decline both collaboration as a duty and class struggle as a cause; they would cooperate where it served them, but reject the corporatist framing.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Stirner scorns the sacred and would not grant heritage inherent value, but he does not call for destroying institutions; split.

dominated-front.rationale: A common front of states is another collective cause and the states involved are opposed by egoism.

workers-nation.rationale: Organizing along class or national lines both subordinate the ego to a collective cause.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Law that fixes roles by sex is a command and a fixed idea; egoists reject both.

ban-interest.rationale: Walker's anarchy regulates business wholly by voluntary contract, which includes lending on agreed terms; a legal ban is a command.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: State classification and separation by race is the state ordering people's lives, which egoists reject in all forms.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Stirner treats the state as a despotism for its own ends, which overlaps with seeing it as an instrument of the dominant, but he does not frame it in class terms.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No egoist doctrine on energy; state production programs would be rejected, but so would state limits.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Demanding that people give up their culture for the nation serves the nation as a sacred cause; the egoist owns their own way of life.

elite-replacement.rationale: Egoists tend to dismiss conspiracy narratives that rest on nation and race as spooks, but state power is a legitimate target of suspicion; no documented position.

proportional-representation.rationale: An electoral mechanism for choosing rulers is no concern of egoists, who reject being bound by any vote.

national-mission.rationale: A national mission is a sacred cause that demands sacrifice from individuals for the nation.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Egoists reject all structures of domination, but they analyze power between individuals, not systematic gender groups; split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Egoists see rulers as pursuing their own interests under moral pretexts, but they would not mourn corruption since all government is despotism.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of state commands over the individual; eugenics postdates The Ego and Its Own.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Egoists recognize no moral or legal right of anyone against power, as right is might; holding a state legally accountable uses state institutions.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Even a minimal state is a despotism for Stirner; egoists want none.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Social or legal discouragement of unions across race is a fixed idea and a restriction on free unions of individuals.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Stirner rejects "Man" and equality as sacred ideals and holds that each is unique with only the rights they can take; he denies equal rights as a moral claim.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Egoists reject the Marxist framework of socialism and revolution as another cause; no position on lasting in one country.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The state is illegitimate, whether settler or not, but egoists don't use the colonial category as a political claim.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Egoists reject state law altogether, so uniformity is not their aim; they also reject religious laws, but would oppose the state imposing either.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Laws on belief are state orders, and Stirner denies that anyone should be bound by religion or its guardians.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A ban expresses a sacred value enforced by law; egoists reject such sacredness and state commands alike.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Egoists reject both state schools and religion, so no religious instruction there is better than the alternative, though they want no state schools at all.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A state that grows stronger is the opposite of the egoist aim, and Stirner rejects any state, including a socialist one.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Stirner denies that even unanimous consent can bind a person, so consent does not legitimise authority, but other individualist anarchists differ.

trade-surplus.rationale: A national trade goal serves the state and nation; egoists do not accept such aims.

population-transfer.rationale: Pressure on a minority to leave is state force over individuals on a collective basis, which egoists reject.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Stirner treats competition as a feature of the liberal society he criticises, while some egoists glorified struggle, so the strands divide.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: A state's power to outlaw parties is a ruling will suppressing opposition; egoists would not defend the constitutional order either.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Egoists reject domination, but treat freedom as less important than ownness and say that the power to interfere matters as power, not as a right; split.

separated-powers.rationale: Division of powers still leaves a state, though checks may be preferable to one despotism; egoists reject the state itself.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined party leading the workers would rule through an idea that possesses individuals.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Stirner denies moral claims by the poor or on their behalf; egoists would leave help to voluntary mutual aid grounded in self-interest.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: State housing and a legal right to buy are both state matters; egoists have no stated view.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Egoists oppose state commands on association and action; strikes and pickets are what individuals may choose to do, so a legal restriction is another order.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Egoism has no theory of poverty; Stirner puts the cause in the lack of power to take, not in numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cohesion of a national society is not an egoist value; individuals form unions on their own interests whatever their origin.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices are still ruling positions; egoists would not choose rulers by any method, though lottery is less offensive than election.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: A state is a despotism with no right to anything, so the egoist denies it any emergency claim on individuals; protections are only worth what power backs them.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price-fixing is a state command overriding voluntary contract, which Walker takes as the regulator of business.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's attack on ruling ideas and censorship; mass and online media postdate the doctrine.

party-commands-army.rationale: Both party and state armies are instruments of rule that egoism rejects.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship is a state status and egoists oppose borders and waiting periods imposed by authority.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Egoists reject representation, but if rulers exist they would not defend high pay; no position beyond the rejection of rule.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Stirner denies that any past decision binds the present self, and he treats party loyalty as possession by an idea.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of every state; supranational unions postdate the doctrine.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Every state is a despotism, whether the despot is a head of state or a legislature.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance matters little, but Stirner rejects religion and clerical authority entirely.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars is rule by the sacred, which Stirner treats as the worst alienation.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Egoists would refuse to sacrifice for the nation and may desert, but they do not adopt a class strategy; the position matches their anti-state stance.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship enforces sacred morality by law; egoists reject both.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits on a ruler are irrelevant to the egoist, who opposes the office altogether.

recall-officials.rationale: Egoists reject representation, so recall has no value for them beyond a tool of power; no position.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliances and foreign garrisons serve states; ending them reduces state power, though egoists would want to end the states.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Walker describes anarchy as voluntary mutual contract, which includes renting; a ban is a state order, and property is what one can hold.

people-in-arms.rationale: Individuals armed and able to assert their power fits the doctrine that right is might, though egoists oppose any mass army and citizen duty.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Stirner does not rate ways of life morally; the claim is a moral ranking the egoist ignores.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunifying a nation serves the nation as a sacred cause; egoists reject nationalism.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No egoist position; Stirner is hostile to intellectuals' ideologies but does not claim educated people are out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Egoists treat cultures as collective spooks, not as having rank; the answer is split between relativism and indifference.

death-penalty.rationale: The state has no right to take life; Stirner says punishment is only the ruler's right and illegalists were its targets.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Egoists reject state schools and their curricula, whether sex education or not; no position.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Egoists reject both state schools and religious dogma, so they do not want creationism in public schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Egoists reject legal restrictions based on moral norms, and treat free conduct as a matter for the individual.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship is a state creation and descent as a claim serves the nation; egoists reject it.

minority-language-support.rationale: State support for languages implies taxation and a state, but egoists would not oppose language use; they reject the program as such.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Egoists reject law and religion; exemptions grant the sacred a claim, though egoists favor relief from laws.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Stirner's ownness is uniqueness against conformity and custom, which he treats as a spook as binding as law.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Egoists reject states and the moral duty to repay; debts are states' affairs and egoists take no side.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Independence for a nation is a spook; egoists do not link it with economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: A democratically elected assembly writing a constitution creates a new ruling will that no egoist is bound by.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: A state restricting individuals for national development serves a sacred cause and a despot.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Duty to the world's poor is moral duty, which Walker calls "the hardened dregs of fear"; egoists give from interest only.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the egoist rejection of state power; nuclear weapons postdate the doctrine.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: A head of state elected by anyone is still a ruler; egoists reject the office and its legitimacy.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A central bank is a state institution; egoists oppose it though not a mandate on prices.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territory held in the name of a nation is a spook and egoists would not defend it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The common good as a test of property is a sacred claim over the owner; property is only one's power.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Egoists regard the USSR as a state tyranny either way; the label is a Marxist debate they do not join.

precautionary-principle.rationale: A state duty to act on risk is a command and a collective cause; egoists have no environmental doctrine.

collective-defense.rationale: A treaty obligation to fight for allies sends individuals to die for states.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The legitimacy of territory is a state matter that egoists reject; they do not argue about consent of a people.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Egoists would weaken the church but reject giving more power to the state; both are masters over the ego.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A head of state as symbol of national unity is a sacred national figure egoists reject.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Force to keep individuals or regions in a state is the despot's tool; egoists favor leaving it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A larger state with autonomous regions is still a state; egoists say nothing on how states divide authority.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred head of state is the clearest spook; Stirner attacks divine right and the sacred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Egoists oppose taxation, flat or not, but a flat tax is less rewarding of state redistribution; no principled position.

character-from-environment.rationale: Stirner focuses on the creative self that owns itself and does not take a side on nature or nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Stirner says law is a declaration of will and the ruler's will is the only effective law; the egoist is not bound by law either, though he doesn't endorse rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: No egoist position; the doctrine is indifferent to goals of civilization.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Any constitution divides rule among ruling bodies; egoists reject all rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Honoring a leader as the embodiment of the nation is the worship of a spook.

equal-parenting.rationale: State presumptions about custody are law, which egoists reject; no position on equal time.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Marxist theory is outside egoism; Stirner opposes both party leaders and the idea of class as cause.

land-redistribution.rationale: Stirner denies that land belongs to the tiller, saying it belongs to whoever can take it; he rejects a state redistribution while accepting seizure by force.

refugee-return.rationale: Egoists recognize no right of return grounded in nation or descent, though they oppose state barriers to movement; no principle either way.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claiming territory for a nationality serves the nation, which Stirner rejects.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving a religion is a sacred law enforced by force, which egoists reject entirely.

women-must-cover.rationale: Laws on dress based on religion or custom bind the individual by a moral command.

common-currency.rationale: Currency arrangements are state matters; egoists favor private money or none but take no side among state arrangements.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: A union of peoples on ancestry is a nationalist cause that egoists reject.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Egoists reject nations as units; self-governing cultural institutions would be preferable to a state, but remain collectivist.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Egoists reject national claims and rights; both options involve a collective struggle that they do not make their own.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Stirner presents history as the history of ideas possessing people, yet the egoist rejects the determinism of material forces over the unique ego.

ban-cartels.rationale: State intervention against economic power overrides voluntary contract; egoists would deal with such power by their own means.

no-bailouts.rationale: State aid taken from taxpayers to prop up firms is an exaction; egoists oppose it though from anti-statism not market principle.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Egoists reject the majority's authority and courts' authority alike; neither binds the individual.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Mandating representation by sex is state command and a collective category; egoists reject public bodies themselves.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: An imperial bloc closed to trade serves the state and nation at the individual's expense.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards from treaties are state commands over exchange; egoists oppose such authority.

moral-incentives.rationale: Walker rejects duty and moral obligation as the basis of conduct and Stirner treats social duty as a spook.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Egoist illegalists and insurrectionists acted without waiting for conditions, but Stirner preferred individual uprising to organized revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Stirner attacks inherited rank as sacred, but he also denies equal rights; egoists would end privilege backed by law and take what they can from it.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Schooling that places a nation or civilization at the center serves a sacred cause egoists reject.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: One society ruling another for its good is rule in the name of Man or progress, a spook.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teaching loyalty and pride toward the nation is instruction in a spook, and Stirner says the patriot's sacrifice profits only the nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Egoists oppose state use of race in either direction and also state anti-discrimination programs; split.

public-money-creation.rationale: State money creation is state power over the economy; egoists oppose it.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Egoism has no theory of capitalism's crises; no position.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence for a former empire serves state and nation, which egoists reject.

delink-world-market.rationale: State policy of national economic separation is a collective program egoists reject; they have no position on trade ties except free contact.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist theory outside egoism; no position.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Voluntary association in both directions is the egoist's basis; Walker holds no one may be compelled in contract or union, so owners and others may refuse.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Stirner denies rights exist beyond power; a written bill is another sacred law over the ego.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Treaties between states bind no one for egoists, but the question is about states and peoples; no position.

elective-rulers.rationale: An elected ruler is still a ruler and a despot; Stirner denies that a vote makes authority legitimate.

minority-veto.rationale: Stirner says even a unanimous decision does not bind the egoist, and a union binds no one without their present will.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Egoists would resist any ruler, though they reject the idea of a trust or constitutional law as ground for it; they resist by interest, not law.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Another sovereign over the individual; Stirner opposes every ruler, including a parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Stirner treats other beings as objects of use and egoism rejects duties toward them; Walker allows sympathy as part of self-interest; split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The egoist would use animals as they see fit, but humane limits are a moral duty they don't recognize; they may follow them from sympathy.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duty of the privileged is moral obligation, rejected by Walker and Stirner alike.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Stirner rejects politics as service of an idea, but his insurrection is also active; adherents differ on withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Stirner sees conformity to the sacred and public opinion as binding people; he does not argue about modern media.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Egoism has no theory of hegemony; Stirner holds rulers rule through people's belief in spooks, which partly fits, but he lacks the class analysis.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices by birth serves the nation and state, which egoists reject entirely.

party-own-road.rationale: Egoists reject communist parties and their lines; the issue is an intra-Marxist question.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: National economic policy is irrelevant to egoism; self-reliance fits personal interest but aid or loans between states are state affairs.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial claims for a nation are a sacred cause egoists reject.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Group descent as ground for political rule is a collective claim and a form of rule; egoists reject both.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Egoists oppose fascism but reject making any value the founding creed of a constitution or state.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Egoists oppose all states and Stirner attacks communist and national causes alike, but equivalence as a condemnation is not a stated position.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical question egoism does not address.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments honor sacred national memory that Stirner rejects, but state removal is also a decree; egoists would not defend them.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Egoists reject programs tied to sex groups and claims of moral duty either way; no position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Egoism has no position; it opposes state-run services but treats violence between individuals as a matter of power.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Egoists reject all state institutions, so no form fits any people; the statement is cultural relativism of forms of rule.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The military ruling as guardian of order is a state despotism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Calls for recognizing work as labor with a state wage rest on moral claims egoists reject; individuals may agree on pay by contract.

filial-duty.rationale: Stirner treats family piety as a sacred tie and fetter, so lifelong duty to parents is a spook.

office-by-exam.rationale: Competitive exams fill the machinery of the state, which egoists oppose.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: State blocking of ownership transfers serves national ends and overrides voluntary exchange.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Egoist unions last only while each member wills them, so ending a marriage needs no fault or permission.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Egoists reject representation, though binding delegates is closer to individual will than free representatives; Stirner denies being bound by vote.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State-mandated accounts are state commands, but egoists favor private provision over state systems; no position.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land held on the community's terms is a collective claim; Stirner says it belongs to whoever can take and hold it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Spending approval by a parliament means a state spending tax money; egoists reject the state's claim to it.

single-official-language.rationale: The state forcing one language on public life is a nationalist order over individuals.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Banning foreigners from land is a state rule on nation lines; Stirner holds land belongs to whoever can take it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: State classification of outcomes by group and its enforcement is a command over individuals egoists reject.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Stirner rejects moral judgment of what one wants; some egoists hold that status chasing is possession by an idea.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: State foreign policy by proxy serves the state; egoists do not support any government's goals.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: A great power invading to hold a bloc together is state despotism over peoples and individuals.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Stirner makes right a matter of power and denies any moral bar on force; Walker accepts self-defense but asserts no rule against initiating force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency theory is outside egoism, which has no account of the world economy; Stirner would blame states and the sacred, not structures.

corporate-influence.rationale: Tucker's strand opposed state-granted monopolies and privileges; inferred as agreement with the claim about influence.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The state is a despot with no claim on the unique individual, so it has no standing to restrict anything.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Stirner treats family and state duties as spooks, so state incentives to breed have no basis; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local authorities are states in miniature with no right to restrict owners; inferred from the critique of the state.

job-guarantee.rationale: Stirner denies that the state can promise or provide any claim on others' labour; individuals deal by contract.

democratic-peace.rationale: Stirner rejects democracy and humanity as spooks, so spreading democracy is not a cause; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Stirner and Walker deny any moral or political obligation to obey law as such; only power and interest bind.

non-intervention.rationale: Rights are only power for egoists, so a rule that nobody has a right to intervene does not fit; they are indifferent.

industrial-unions.rationale: Egoists form shifting voluntary unions of their own choosing, not fixed industry structures; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: egoists disregard collective guilt and the nation as a spook, so no one conspires against it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Stirner attacks marriage and family as spooks, and egoist anarchists apply unions of egoists to sex and romance.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Egoists would take any information they can, and secrecy shields the state; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Egoists set no norm of production, only own interest; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Egoists favour shifting voluntary unions with no permanent organisation or binding duty.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Stirner dismisses both nationalism and law as spooks, so national law has no priority.

religious-nation.rationale: Stirner attacks nationalism and religion as spooks claiming the individual.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Stirner rejects any sacred authority above the ego, so ritual submission and tribute to a leading power is ruled out.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: egoists reject the state entirely, so regional pooling or retention is irrelevant to them.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: Stirner treats property as what one can take and keep, not a right of either individuals or the commons.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: egoists oppose the state in every form, but they do not make defeating communism a cause because causes are not owed their concern.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: egoists reject the state, so publicly funded systems are not a concern; a union of egoists could use any provider.

religion-illusion.rationale: Stirner argues that religion is a spook in the mind that people serve, treating God as a fixed idea; he does not tie it to material conditions.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: Stirner does not assess capitalism historically; Tucker's strand attacks monopoly while accepting the market.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: egoists reject all fixed causes including feminism as a spook, though they oppose legal subordination of any person.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: egoists reject compulsory public provision; voluntary arrangements are permitted.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: Stirner owns language as his own to use, and no authority may impose a purge.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: a treaty binds only while each party wills it, so no fixed obligation holds beyond that.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: egoists accept voluntary unions of egoists but reject a society reorganised around any common project.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of state power and national causes as spooks.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: egoists reject both state capitalism and communism as claims over the individual, but they do not offer a single third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Stirner treats property as what one can take and keep and calls nationalism a spook, so no people's historical tie to land confers a right (s1).

holocaust-denial.rationale: Egoism has no doctrine on historical events; an egoist has no interest in a falsehood and nothing in the sources supports denial, so this is inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Egoists reject law and moral duty as spooks, and Wikipedia notes unions of egoists applied to sex and romance, so no act between consenting adults is a crime.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Stirner opposes the state as despotism and holds that only individuals' own power counts; suppression for 'order' is the rule of a spook (inferred from s1, s3).

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Stirner attacks God and religion as spooks and denies that any state or law may bind the ego, so a state punishing blasphemy has no standing.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the egoist rejection of state and nation as claimants on anyone; colonial rule is not discussed.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Egoists deny any religious or moral duty binding the individual (Walker), though resisting invaders for one's own interest is allowed; the statement's obligation is what is rejected.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Egoists deny that any ruler is legitimate, religious or not, and favour revolt for one's own interest, but not to impose religious law; inferred and split.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Stirner dismisses democracy as another form of rule over the individual, though egoists accept voluntary unions in which each takes part directly; the decision-by-community framing is not their goal.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Stirner rejects collective categories and 'humanity' as spooks and focuses on the individual's own power, so the framing is not theirs; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Egoists reject state recognition and legal categories as claims on the ego, though each person may define themselves; the statement asks for legal recognition, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: The ego owns its own life and no moral law or state may forbid ending it; professionals may help by voluntary contract (inferred from s1, s2).

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Egoists reject both liberal and communist creeds as spooks but do not frame this as a synthesis of left and right; adherents would not obviously take a side.

alienated-labor.rationale: Stirner criticises the communist glorification of labour and holds that work should serve one's own ends, but he does not use an alienation theory; adherents are split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Egoists treat all religions and nations as spooks and reject collective cultural claims; inferred from Stirner's critique of national and religious identity.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Stirner's central claim is that God, state and humanity are spooks and that right is only power, so authority from God is rejected.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Egoists reject state religion, but also dislike state rules on personal dress; mildly negative by inference since they want no state institutions to bind individuals.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Egoists reject legal prohibitions and favour freely made contracts (Walker), though they back individuals' defence of themselves; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Egoists reject the state's role in either regulation or welfare in favour of voluntary contract (Walker); social protection through the state is the compulsion they deny.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Egoists want no state and so no state army, though individuals may arm in self-defence (Walker); inferred, since they do not argue it as pacifism.

rich-first.rationale: Property is what one can take and keep and each pursues their own gain, so unequal results are accepted, though they do not endorse stepwise development; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Egoists owe no loyalty to any state or bloc and act only in their own interest, but they have no foreign-policy programme; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Stirner rejects any ruler or state office, so hereditary succession of a state leader has no standing; inferred from his denial of the state.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Stirner's union of egoists allows any voluntary dealing, but he mocks fixed principles about credit; adherents like Tucker backed mutual banks while Stirner did not address it.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from rejecting the state's claims: egoists owe no obedience to lenders' terms imposed through a government, though they would not frame it as a duty of government.

property-franchise.rationale: Stirner denies the state any claim to rule, and a property qualification would make a state's franchise a privilege of owners; inferred from his rejection of the state and of voting rights.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Egoists treat 'nature' and 'woman' as spooks with no claim on the ego, so the linkage is neither endorsed nor opposed; inferred from Stirner's rejection of fixed ideas.

reification.rationale: Stirner attacks ideas that come to rule over people as spooks, which resembles reification, but he does not discuss capitalism in these terms.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Tucker and Walker held that formal liberties are hollow without the means to use them, and Stirner calls the liberal freedom of the press a freedom granted by the state; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Egoists hold law is only power and reject being bound by any ruler's statutes, so announced standing laws carry no authority; inferred, though they prefer rule by known law to arbitrary decree in practice.

racial-franchise.rationale: Egoism denies any group or racial collective a claim on the individual and rejects the state, so a racial franchise is a spook-based privilege.

online-participation.rationale: Stirner never addressed it; egoists would use any tool for their own ends but reject binding collective decisions, so split.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed by egoists, who reject the state and its record-keeping alike; transparency would matter only as a tool for the individual.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Stirner rejects religion and the state's claim to regulate unions of individuals, so a law restricting marriage between faiths is an unjustified imposition.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Egoists reject group-based hatred as a spook, though each person may avoid whatever shops they please; inferred from his view that humanity and religion carry no claim.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Stirner treats any collective decision that binds the individual as another sovereign over the ego; a lot-chosen body is still a body whose verdict is imposed, so an egoist would prefer voluntary unions (inferred, he never discussed it).

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Stirner holds that no doctrine binds the owner of himself, so each person may rework inherited teaching freely, though he thinks even liberal theology keeps a sacred fixed idea (inferred).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Stirner dismisses liberty as a cause owed to anyone and Tucker's strand blamed state-backed monopolies for concentrated wealth; the question is not addressed directly, so this is inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Stirner denies the state's right to bar or compel anyone, so a ban has no standing, though he would reject military service as a duty; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Stirner treats the state and atheist humanism alike as spooks that claim the individual, so state-taught unbelief would be one more imposed creed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Stirner attacks punishment and the state's monopoly of force, and Walker allows self-defence by individuals, so safety would come from voluntary arrangements.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Egoists reject rule by any community or majority; guaranteed shares of power would still be government over individuals. Inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Egoists want no state welfare and treat helping others as self-interest freely chosen, so private help is preferred; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Egoists regard all elected office as the state's business and are largely indifferent to how long politicians serve.

vote-delegation.rationale: Stirner rejects representation and handing one's will to others as a violation of ownness; delegating a vote would be a surrender of it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: No cause, including humanity's survival, has a claim on the ego; inferred from Stirner's denial of duty to any abstraction.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Egoists see religious office as a spook with no authority to reserve roles by sex; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Stirner treats the family and authority within it as non-sacred, with relations resting on each party's will; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; Stirner treats citizenship as a spook, but he also scorns voting and the state, so egoists have no settled view on extending a state vote.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; rent caps are state coercion in the name of a social ideal, while egoists want exchange by voluntary agreement among the parties.

abolish-ip.rationale: Adherents are split: Stirner's view of property as what one can hold undermines legal monopolies, but Tucker defended patents and copyright.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Stirner treats the nation as a spook and calls on the individual not to serve it, so drilled youth movements for national service would be rejected.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; egoists reject every state's claims alike, so where weapons are kept is not a matter of principle.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed; egoists give no state authority, domestic or foreign, so foreign bases raise no principle of their own.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Stirner's critique of state moral claims, so official state recognition is a moral gesture an egoist would not value.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Stirner attacks the holy status of labour in communism and holds that property is what one can take and keep, so no claim about what income should reward holds for him.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Walker rejects moral duty and allows self-defence, and Stirner holds that no moral law binds the individual, so killing an attacker is not wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Stirner treats nationalism as a spook and the nation as no claim on the individual, so an unbroken national identity is a fiction.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Stirner's rejection of fixed essences and generic categories as spooks.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of general categories like Man in favour of the unique individual, so a fixed category of women would be a spook too.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Stirner treats the nation and sacrifice for causes as spooks, so sacred honours for national dead are fixed-idea veneration.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Stirner mocks the spooks and fixed ideas that cast politics as a struggle for sacred causes and holds that only the individual's interest counts.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; Stirner rejects the nation as a spook, so homeland questions are outside egoist concern.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; both nation-building by culture and by state are claims over the individual, so egoists take neither side.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; Stirner treats God as a spook, so how to describe God is of no concern to egoists.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Stirner and SEP treat the standard of humanity as another spook, so judging texts by the full humanity of women is just another higher essence.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Stirner rejects nationalism and holds that the state is despotism, so a national-majority claim over economic life has no standing.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the denial of state authority and of peoples as spooks, so no state unit should be drawn for a people.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the denial of political obligation: groups of egoists would be self-run, but Stirner offers no union programme.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Stirner rejects both state and communist creeds as spooks, so the definition of socialism is not his concern.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Only the unique individual has claims; the community or state owning local essentials is a spook, and services would be supplied by voluntary union.

second-chamber.rationale: Stirner rejects the state, its law and its legislature as claims over the individual.

municipal-property.rationale: Property is what one can take and keep, and the local community has no claim any more than the state does.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Egoists reject assemblies that decide for individuals, though shifting voluntary unions of egoists coordinating are accepted; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Walker's egoism rests on contract and individual interest, so pay is settled by the bargain and not by the family's needs.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the egoist view that individuals are their own masters and state regulation has no claim on them.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from rejection of taxation and state claims on the individual, though egoists might fund it in a union.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the view that the state has no right over an individual's power, which includes how they trade.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the view that no one owes the state or society an account of themselves, so a pseudonym is the egoist's own business.

person-over-state.rationale: Split: the state serves nobody on the egoist view, but egoists themselves treat others as means to their own ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Stirner treats spirit, God and humanity as spooks and fixed ideas, and denies politics any duty to serve them.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Rejects all government, national and regional alike, so neither version of the arrangement is wanted; inferred as neutral.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; the individual's interest sets the standard and the issue is a matter of taste.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; environmental arguments are not an egoist standard.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Stirner treats nation, race and humanity as collective spooks with no claim over the unique individual.

racial-pride.rationale: Stirner's critique of nationalism covers pride in nation or race as an attachment to a spook.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Egoists owe the state nothing and its wars are rejected, but they accept self-defence and shifting unions, so the statement fits only partly.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Stirner treats nation, like state and humanity, as a spook with no claim on the unique individual, so a shared language does not make a people one nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Egoism rejects representation and religious or collective bodies claiming the individual's will; Stirner holds that no one can speak for the ego.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of nationalism: 'my country' is a spook, so a partition plot is no concern of an egoist, though states' schemes are taken as expected power-seeking.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's view that the state is a despotism funded by taxation; an egoist would want education arranged by voluntary union, not tax-funded.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from egoist rejection of the state's taxing power; any needed limits on pollution would come from the injured parties' own power and agreements.

future-generations.rationale: Duty to humanity or posterity is a moral spook for Stirner; the egoist owes nothing to anyone and acts only from own interest.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of collective claims and fixed essences; no group is entitled to extra weight in public life, and egoists reject public life as state business.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: egoists reject the state and its armaments but only as one power among others; individuals may arm themselves, so adherents have no common view on state arms levels.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: egoists oppose the state and care little how governments conduct diplomacy; secrecy is no more a violation of any claim than openness.

capital-controls.rationale: Egoism holds that property is what one can take and keep, with no state claim to control it; state control of capital movement is state coercion over the owner's power.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Stirner calls the state a despotism and denies it any claim on the individual, so a state monopoly of arms has no standing.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Stirner denies that the state can command an individual, so a soldier may refuse; but egoists reject duties, so they would call it a choice, not a duty.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; egoists may join unions or contract alone as their interest dictates and prescribe neither.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: taxation funds the state that egoists reject, and a state top-up is a claim of society on others.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: egoists want to bind no one by law, but legal limits on a state's borrowing would still be preferable to none.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: rules for an international economy assume collective claims of nations and states, which egoists treat as spooks.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: Stirner opposes both taking over the state and founding a new order, preferring insurrection that arranges nothing in advance, so neither wording fits.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Egoists leave arrangements to shifting voluntary unions and Walker and Tucker allowed markets and sharing, so no fixed blueprint is imposed.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; nature is only something an ego may use, which does not settle whether it should be priced.

sacred-nation.rationale: Stirner treats the nation and nationalism as spooks that have no claim on the unique individual.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: relief by public action is a state act, though debtors may owe nothing by egoist reasoning.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: egoists reject collective categories such as regions and hold exploitation to be between individuals, not between territories.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Stirner rejects 'Man' and a shared essence as a spook that grounds rights and dignity, holding that only the unique individual counts.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: state funding of any media rests on the state and compulsory taxes that egoists reject.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Stirner treats God and sacred creeds as spooks that claim the ego, so no religion's truth binds the egoist, and he gives no reason to rank them as one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Stirner calls the state a despotism, so a state-guaranteed price or public credit scheme is a claim on others that an egoist would refuse.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Stirner never addressed weapons; since he holds that right is only power, an egoist would not give up power unilaterally. Inferred from that principle.

workers-own-party.rationale: Stirner rejects parties, the state and the cause of labour as spooks, so an egoist has no place for a class party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Egoists reject law and the state as such, so a criminal ban is not their tool, though they also reject custom as a binding authority. Inferred from that.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Egoists reject legal rights granted by the state and equally reject custom that binds anyone, so they are neither for nor against; inferred from Stirner's view that property is what one can take and keep.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Stirner never addressed this and an egoist has no stake in what a nation or region calls its language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Egoists reject courts and law as state instruments, so they would leave pollution disputes to the parties' own power or voluntary agreement, not liability law. Inferred from Stirner's critique of law.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Stirner attacks inherited authority and sacred tradition as spooks, so chiefs with an official role in law have no claim on the egoist.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Stirner denies that nature, humanity or any cause is owed the ego's interest, so freedom does not yield to an environmental duty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Stirner rejects law and punishment as the state's claim over the individual, so he would reject fixed state sentences.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Stirner denies the state and the nation any claim on the individual, so a state requirement on immigrants has no basis.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Stirner denies any claim of society or association on the individual, so a union may not be imposed on a worker; egoists join only voluntary unions of egoists.

voter-id.rationale: Egoists reject the state and its claims of citizenship, so a state ID and citizenship requirement for voting has no legitimacy for them.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of any sacred authority; no interpretation of a religion has a claim, and the state has no business giving one precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Stirner rejects the state and representative government as a ruler over the unique one, so a government elected in free votes is no less a despotism.

premarital-sex.rationale: Egoists hold morality and marriage to be spooks with no claim on the individual, so a woman's sexual conduct is her own affair.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The egoist state has no right to rule at all, and cutting off people's communication to keep order is a clear exercise of power over them.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of the state and taxation; a state cash payment rests on state coercion, though it is less objectionable than programs run by the state.

women-suffrage.rationale: Stirner held that no one has rights beyond their power and rejected state office and voting alike, so equal rights to vote and hold office are not a demand he makes.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's treatment of God and religion as spooks that bind the individual; not specifically about women.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of fixed essences and of 'Man' as a spook; no source states a view on race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Egoists reject the state and its bureaucracies of any kind, so a state agency for any goal has no legitimacy.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Stirner holds that property is whatever the individual can take and keep by power, so an earlier claim creates no right; no one owns by moral title.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Rejects any court or ruler as holding a claim over the individual, since right is only power; an international tribunal is one more spook.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Stirner treats God and sacred texts as spooks that have no claim on the unique one; they are not authoritative, still less inerrant.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Stirner's rejection of collective rights and guarantees imposed from above, though he has no objection to women acting for themselves.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Denies the state any claim whatever, planned or not; a bureaucratic state is still a state to be opposed, not defended.

indirect-election.rationale: Rejects rulers and offices altogether, so any ladder of delegates filling higher office is rejected as another form of rule.

national-church-status.rationale: Rejects the state and church as spooks and any privileged institutional status for one religion.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its rejection of states of any size, so autonomy within a state does not satisfy it, though it would let any group separate.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its rejection of the claim that nations or states have a right to a people, so a vote does not settle who belongs where.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its view that borders and states are spooks, so there is no reason to respect colonial lines as binding.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its principle that each pursues their own interest and enjoyment, which is not an ascetic or limited-needs ideal.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its rejection of any authority controlling where individuals may go or settle.

equal-conscription.rationale: Rejects conscription as the state's claim on the person; equal or unequal, the claim is itself denied.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Stirner treats the nation and the fatherland as spooks that have no claim on the unique individual, so no duty to a homeland exists.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Egoist anarchism rejects the state and its law altogether, and Stirner calls the state a despotism, so no state may kill anyone.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that an egoist anarchist has no stake in what states do and would call the question moot.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Stirner dismisses the nation as a spook, so a state owes nothing to people of its nation abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Stirner holds that property is what one can take and keep, so no equal claim of everyone to resources exists.

self-ownership.rationale: Stirner's ownness makes the individual their own owner and the only owner of their power and labour.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from rejecting the state's claim on the individual, which would include its power to tax.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed; an egoist would reject state social spending of any kind as resting on the state.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from rejecting every ruler and every leader's claim to embody the people.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from opposition to the state and its law, which rules out special legal privileges for anyone.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of religion and of every fixed idea as a ground for politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Stirner calls tradition and sacred ideas spooks that bind the individual, so a return to ancestral values is no goal.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the view that no law or husband holds binding authority over a person's will.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the denial that the nation is a unit with claims, so national control means nothing in itself.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Stirner treats justice and right as spooks, so neither process nor pattern makes a distribution just; inferred from that stance.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's view of the state as a despotism with no claim on the individual's property, so it may not tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Stirner dismissed race and humanity as abstractions with no claim; the sources do not address it, so adherents are indifferent.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Stirner holds that no law binds the ego, just or unjust, so this is agreed in outcome though not in terms of justice; inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's critique of work as a calling and his preference for the individual's own enjoyment over labour.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from the denial that any single sovereign has a claim on the unique one; not addressed directly.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Stirner rejects labour as the source of right, though Tucker, who took up egoism, held a cost-of-labour view, so adherents are not wholly agreed.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's treatment of nation as a spook with no claim on the ego.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: Stirner disparaged both class and identity causes as claims on the ego, so egoists are indifferent.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of any party or state rule over individuals.

missingStatements.text: Rights are nothing more than what a person has the power to take and defend.
missingStatements.rationale: Stirner writes that what you have the power to be you have the right to, and Walker that he has a right to do what he can take and openly keep.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to egoist/might-is-right thought; individual-rights-only and self-interest-moral capture the substance.

missingStatements.text: No one has a moral duty to put the interests of others before their own.
missingStatements.rationale: Walker calls moralistic duty the hardened dregs of fear and Stirner denies that any cause is owed his concern.

missingStatements.text: An agreement or association should bind its members only for as long as each of them still wants it.
missingStatements.rationale: Stirner's union of egoists is renewed by each member's present will, and he denies that a past decision binds the present self.

notes: Egoism is a philosophy of the individual more than a political program, so many policy answers are inferred (low). Tucker-style contract anarchists and Nietzschean might-makes-right writers would answer some economic and violence items differently.
